title: Roha fatality inquiry to resume Friday
article: The inquiry into the death of Tamer Sayed Roha, who died two years ago in police custody, will resume Friday after skipping today.

Testimony from the last witness was postponed when he failed to show up on time Wednesday. He arrived shortly after proceedings had been adjourned. Provincial court Judge Anne Brown decided to have the witness come back Friday rather than hear his testimony in the absence of key participants.
Earlier, a police officer and two paramedics told the inquiry what they saw and did Sept. 4, 2002, when Roha died after being handcuffed.
Police arrested the 27-year-old man when he began screaming and behaving erratically at a northwest motel. Toxicology reports showed Roha had high levels of cocaine in his system.
